title: Fold TensorAxis sort fallback into one validation pass
masterplan_authority: Revision 11 / Version 2.2.0 / Gate 1 — Renovation and owner-directed Genesis
finding: TensorAxis exact canonical tuples were already retained by object identity, but an out-of-order exact tuple validated a prefix until the first ordering violation and then routed the entire bounded sequence through _sorted_strings. That fallback revalidated the already-seen prefix, allocated a duplicate-detection set, sorted, and materialized a replacement tuple. Adding a cache, label index, adapter, or second axis representation would increase rather than reduce the surface.
primary_claim: TensorAxis now performs bounded label validation and order detection in one traversal, retains an exact already-canonical tuple unchanged, and sorts only when canonical ordering is actually required. Invalid, duplicate, NUL-containing, and oversized inputs remain fail closed. Fourfold authority, TensorView wire semantics, digest semantics, and projection status semantics are unchanged.
gardener_decision: Fold the non-canonical sort fallback into the same bounded validation traversal instead of adding a parallel label representation. The exact canonical tuple remains the single immutable representation; only inputs that actually require ordering allocate a temporary list for sorting. This removes the duplicate validation path without broadening the Tensor/Fourfold architecture.
acceptance: an unsorted exact TensorAxis label tuple is canonicalized deterministically while each label receives semantic non-empty validation exactly once
an exact already-canonical TensorAxis label tuple remains eligible for object-identity reuse through the existing contract surface
